clue.text: Shy person in taxi stifling expression of pain

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, so one piece closes round the other

parts.note: a taxi's passenger is its fare
ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: A timid cab passenger tries to suppress a cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived adjective describes someone sullenly timid and unsociable, which is to say shy.

clue.text: Subversive saint, remarkably hiding cunning

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hide the other piece within them
remarkably suggests something altered out of the ordinary, so the letters of saint are rearranged

parts.note: arch means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: A holy man is surprisingly concealing his slyness and plotting revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint is no holy figure but raw letters: 'remarkably' rearranges them to ANIST, which 'hiding' wraps round the word for sly.
explanation.definitionFit: A subversive is one who seeks to overthrow authority, as an anarchist does.

clue.text: Herb Cordelia's sister stuffed into a couple of ducks

indicators.note: one piece is stuffed inside the other

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O, so two ducks are OO
Regan is one of Cordelia's sisters in Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.surface: A cook stuffs a pair of ducks with a herb named after a Shakespearean princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic culinary herb, wild marjoram.

clue.text: Officer in charge is a severe pain

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: Having an officer in command is agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe spasmodic abdominal pain.

clue.text: European project that can't get off the ground

definitions.meaning: European Monetary Union, the scheme for a single currency

definitions.text: that can't get off the ground
definitions.meaning: a flightless bird, which cannot take off

explanation.definitionFit: The letters abbreviate European Monetary Union and also name the large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Cramp admitted by grim pedestrian

indicators.note: what is admitted by the words sits inside them, so the letters are found within grim pedestrian

explanation.surface: A gloomy walker has let a muscle spasm in.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp someone is to restrict or hinder them, a verb sense synonymous with obstruct.

clue.text: Sort of crime that an office worker experiences?

definitions.text: Sort of crime that an office worker experiences?

parts.words: Sort of crime that an office worker experiences?
parts.note: a crime committed with help from someone on the staff, read literally as the employment of someone working indoors at a desk

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a crime done by or with a trusted employee, and literally an indoor post.

clue.text: Quickly coming to new town in Lancashire

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a quick tempo

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to a new town in the north-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.

clue.text: A number practise a form of Buddhism

parts.note: to do something is to practise or perform it
Zen is a school of Mahayana Buddhism

explanation.surface: Several people take up a branch of Buddhist meditation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is twelve, a specific number.

clue.text: Come to wash

definitions.meaning: to regain consciousness or rouse from sleep
the disturbed water left behind a moving boat

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is rousing from sleep; the other is the trail of churned water behind a vessel.

clue.text: Like certain furniture Frenchman wants to get hold of?

parts.note: Louis is a typical French man's name
to seize is to grab or get hold of

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is keen to grab some antique furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, Louis wants to seize; but seize is also French for sixteen, so the phrase names Louis XVI, whose period gives a style of French furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Seize names the late eighteenth-century French decorative style of the reign of Louis XVI, used of furniture.

clue.text: Upstart providing wild rave-up for any number to enter

indicators.note: a letter that enters another word is put inside it
wild means unruly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: n stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A newcomer throws a riotous party open to all comers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns RAVEUP into PARVEU, and 'to enter' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone newly risen to wealth or status, an upstart.

clue.text: Girl initially expressing Thatcherite principle

definitions.meaning: the initial letters of 'There is no alternative', a slogan of Margaret Thatcher's governments

explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister 1979-90, was associated with the slogan 'There is no alternative', abbreviated by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short female forename and also the acronym of the Thatcher-era slogan about no alternative existing.

clue.text: Old-fashioned type ruins a do that's swinging

indicators.note: something swinging is moving about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some square spoils a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur, figuratively, is a person stuck in outdated ways, an old-fashioned fogey.

clue.text: We turned up escaping out of armies twice for let-up from war

indicators.note: letters escaping out of the words leave them, so they are removed
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: We give up and slip away from two armies, glad of a pause in fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes EW of We; removing E then W from ARMIESTWICE leaves ARMIS TICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, a cessation of hostilities in a war.

clue.text: Winter month and what it may bring for girl

parts.note: Jan is the short form of January, a winter month in the north
January may bring ice

explanation.surface: January and its frosts are named as the inspiration for a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female forename, so it fits the general word for a girl.

clue.text: Conservative on a par with former President

parts.note: level means equal, on a par
and means together with

explanation.surface: A Tory is equal in standing to a past head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was twice President of the United States, in the 1880s and 1890s.

clue.text: One small river and another beset by vapour

indicators.note: to be beset by something is to be surrounded by it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: steam is water vapour
another river, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A little river and a second one are wreathed in mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' follows 'river', so it means another river, given by the usual abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a brook, a small flowing river.

clue.text: Animated old lover summoned to court

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to be cited is to be summoned before a court

explanation.surface: A former partner is called to give evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means lively and stirred up, close in sense to animated.

clue.text: Welcomes couple into German town

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany
a brace is a pair or couple

explanation.surface: A pair arrive in a German town and are greeted warmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hug or welcome them, a synonym in the third person singular.

clue.text: When to resign? Hard for a PM

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to quit is to resign
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister wonders when to step down, finding it difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was British Prime Minister from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Heroic English copper Head of Interpol brought in

indicators.note: a letter brought in is placed inside the policeman's abbreviation

parts.note: a copper is a police constable, PC

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brave English policeman calls in the chief of the international police.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes deeds on a heroic, grand scale, as in an epic poem.

clue.text: Spaniard is old man facing endless misfortune

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a blow is a setback or misfortune

explanation.surface: A Spanish father faces a run of bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo is a typical Spanish man's name, as in Picasso.

clue.text: Nickname that could make bloke initially quite sour

indicators.note: the letters could make a new word when rearranged
initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being given a nickname might turn a man rather bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubriquet is a familiar name or epithet given to someone, a variant spelling of sobriquet.

clue.text: Stiff attire notion half forgotten

parts.note: rig is clothing, an outfit

indicators.note: half of the word is forgotten, so only its first half is kept

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: Formal dress is a concept only half remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unbending, stiff.

clue.text: Not allowing anyone to get cross?

definitions.text: Not allowing anyone to get cross?

parts.words: Not allowing anyone to get cross?
parts.note: reads like refusing to let people get angry, but the cross is the mark on a ballot paper, so it describes declining to vote for any candidate

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains in an election marks no cross by any name, giving no candidate a vote.

clue.text: Gershwin song that endlessly came up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A Gershwin number that kept rising without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ARIA to ARI, and 'came up' turns it to give the lyricist brother of George Gershwin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of composer George Gershwin.

clue.text: Boy about five was a terrible tyrant

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it

parts.note: Ian is a boy's name
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A lad of about five years old was a dreadful bully.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing phrase: Ivan IV of Russia was known as the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible, the sixteenth-century tsar, is the classic terrible tyrant of history.

clue.text: Dog died in Dorset town

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: Poole is a port town in Dorset, a county in southern England
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dog passed away in a south-coast town.
explanation.definitionFit: The poodle is a breed of dog with a curly coat.

clue.text: Organic compound is possibly deadly, eh?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist wonders whether a certain organic compound might be lethal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldehyde is a class of organic chemical containing a CHO group, such as formaldehyde.
